- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak or use 20-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) or shows strong bearish signals, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% buffer to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model exhibits lag in reacting to sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns bearish after 3–5 days, adjust forecast downward by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility; apply smoothing (e.g., 7-day EWMA) to reduce noise and avoid overreaction to short-term sentiment swings.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model tends to err on the side of bullish; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5-day mean to anchor forecast.
